turns.text: why does a system with many interacting parts settle into a stable pattern instead of staying chaotic
because the interactions impose constraints; the system relaxes toward the lowest-energy configuration consistent with them, and symmetry breaking picks one stable state out of many
so the stability comes from the constraints not from the parts themselves
right, the collective order is a property of the coupling. remove the constraints and it returns to disorder. the order is emergent, it is not in any single part
and a small perturbation can push it to a different stable state
yes, a critical perturbation crosses a threshold and the whole system reorganizes into a new attractor. below threshold it absorbs the noise
